provisions.summary: Raises the cigarette and little cigar tax from 16 to 21 cents each, on and after January 1, 2026. The spec models the cigarette part only; the little cigar part is not modeled.
provisions.approximation: The bill taxes little cigars at the same 21 cents, but the spec models cigarettes only. The estimate is therefore slightly too low, by the little cigar revenue.
provisions.quote: 21.00 cents for each cigarette or little cigar sold, used, or possessed by a wholesaler or dealer on and after January 1, 2026

provisions.summary: Changes how cigarette tax revenue is divided among special funds (25% or a dollar cap each to the cancer research, trauma system, community health centers and emergency medical services funds). The excess goes to the general fund. This is an allocation, not a tax change.
provisions.quote: twenty-five per cent or $14,080,000, whichever is less, shall be deposited to the credit of the Hawaii cancer research special fund

notes: Effective-date conflict: section 4 says the Act takes effect July 1, 2025, but the new 21-cent rate applies on and after January 1, 2026. I used the rate's own date, 2026-01-01, as 'effective'. Both dates are in the past as of today (2026-11-27), so a reviewer should confirm the start date and how much of the first year to count. Section 1 also repeals old historical cigarette rates, which are obsolete and change nothing. The fund allocations in section 2 (beginning July 1, 2025, with the excess carrying to the general fund) do not change the estimate. The bill's title and description mention expanding the allocation to all tobacco product taxes, but the section 2 text I was given deposits percentages of all moneys collected under chapter 245, so it does reach other tobacco taxes. That is still only an allocation. The 70% and 50% tobacco product rates in section 1 are unchanged from current law.
